data.title: Documentation in the journal: how it works
body: What it is: the current account of something (a module, a contract, a process). Revised; readers get the latest. A note is a moment and never changes; a decision is a choice with a reason. Neither is this.
Where it lives: .kadence/events as doc.written (one whole revision: title, body, parents) and doc.linked (explains a task). No .md file is created. ADR-014.
kadence doc edit DOC-N --body "…"      earlier revisions stay in the journal
kadence prime                   names documentation of the work you hold
kadence task show KAD-N --json  documentation[]: label, title, bytes — no bodies
kadence doc list --json         the index, no bodies
kadence doc show DOC-N --json   one body

Conflicts: two revisions on top of the same one (two branches) are both kept. show gives the latest and lists the other under conflicts. Settle it by writing the merged text; an edit without text is refused (conflicting_state).
Keep it short: past 16 KiB a document is written with a warning. Agents read long text worse; one document per topic.
Before anyone runs compact: everyone updates. kadence 0.5.0 and earlier delete doc.* events when they compact a month.
